description: Equipo enfocado en desarrollar soluciones de comunicación resiliente para misiones lunares y exploración espacial profunda. Nuestro objetivo: crear un sistema que mantenga la señal estable aunque se interrumpa el enlace con la Tierra, detectando y aislando en tiempo real interferencias por radiación y ruido espacial. Trabajamos con arquitectura ligera, autónoma, sin dependencias externas, buscando llevar estabilidad y seguridad a cada etapa de la misión.
summary:
GÉNESIS-GAL OS is an autonomous, spectral-architecture operating system built from the ground up in Guatemala, featuring an executable kernel of just 89 Kilobytes.

The project addresses the critical challenge of operational autonomy and mission continuity during communication blackouts at the lunar South Pole and in deep space. In regions where lunar terrain or vast distances block direct signals with Earth, probes and rovers cannot wait for human commands or risk having traditional operating systems crash or corrupt data due to cosmic radiation.

To solve this, GÉNESIS-GAL OS replaces legacy 1980s computing foundations through three core innovations: it substitutes the Von Neumann architecture with phase resonance and continuous states; eliminates vulnerable disk allocation tables via FASEFS3 (using per-record CRC checksums and a self-healing Spectral Root Node to safeguard every byte of telemetry offline); and integrates a 5th-Order Kalman Filter Stabilization Engine that corrects 99.9994% of system instability in real time without freezing or rebooting.
details:
GÉNESIS-GAL OS: Project Details and Technical Vision

1. What does it do or how does it work? GÉNESIS-GAL OS is an ultra-lightweight aerospace kernel with a bare-metal architecture (~127 KB) designed to run directly on the motherboard without dependencies on traditional operating systems (such as Windows or Linux). Rather than relying on the traditional binary Boolean logic (0 and 1) used for the past 70 years, it introduces a computational model based on phase resonance and continuous state. It features a resilient file system with dual-zone redundancy, CRC32 verification, direct GPT/MBR support at the LBA level, and an independent network stack (Layer 2) for low-latency autonomous telecommunications.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Deterministic performance: Full control over processor cycles with automatic thermal and phase stability calibration.
  • Minimal footprint: A complete operating kernel compressed into approximately 127 KB.
  • Warm Start State: Ability to instantaneously recover the prior state of mathematical coherence across reboots.
  • Mission resilience: Robust deep-space communication links through synchronization with the Deep Space Network (DSN) and continuous state estimation.

3. What is the expected impact of the project? GÉNESIS-GAL OS redefines deep-space computing, delivering ultra-low latency and deterministic reliability for next-generation flight computers, planetary landers, and autonomous satellite constellations. It breaks away from bloated operating systems, ensuring safe execution of critical missions in extreme environments.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop the project?

  • Base architecture and kernel: Low-level systems programming (Assembly / C / bare-metal Rust targeting UEFI).
  • Analytical engine: 5th-order Kalman Filter algorithm coupled with physical matrices for real-time state estimation.
  • Visualization: Interactive vector HUD projecting celestial bodies (Earth, Moon, Sun) and real-time orbital trajectory simulation.
  • Hardware: Tested and compiled as a Release Candidate directly on the final target hardware.

5. In what sense is your project creative? The project introduces a paradigm shift by moving away from standard binary logic through continuous-state phase resonance models, fusing advanced aerospace mathematics directly into a lightweight UEFI-bootable environment.

6. What factors did your team take into account?

  • Reliability and safety: Elimination of non-deterministic runtime garbage collection and the overhead of heavy operating systems.
  • Interplanetary constraints: Power management, DSN synchronization, and immediate recovery (warm start) under severe hardware and thermal limitations.
